To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified the G17V mutation of RHOA in 50–75% of angio-immunoblastic T cell lymphoma (AIT) cases, and that this mutation activates the TCR signaling pathway via VAV1.

we discovered the G17V mutant RHOA as a novel binding partner to VAV1, which augmented its adaptor function by phosphorylation of 1 74Tyr, resulting TCR signaling acceleration, which may be a new therapeutic target of AITL.
G17V RhoA mutation inactivates the canonical RhoA signaling, and instead, it forms a novel complex with Vav1, which augments the T cell receptor signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new signaling axis in AITL and the discovery of its therapeutic implications.
the discovery of a novel function of the somatic G17V RhoA mutant in the activation of Vav1 signaling in angiolimmunoblastic t-cell lymphoma.
the identification of the G17 V RHOA-VAV1 axis in AITL, a new therapeutic target for the treatment of AITL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G17V RHA activates TCR signaling via binding to VAV1, and that this is a novel mechanism of T-cell lymphomagenesis.
the RHOA–G17V mutation is a novel driver mutation for the AITL and the VAV1–174Tyr phosphorylating kinase is an important target for the treatment of the AITL.
the G17 V RHOA–mediated activation of the VAV1–TCR signaling axis plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of AITL and may serve as a therapeutic target for AITL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

G17V RHA mutation is a driver mutation in angioimmuno-blatic T-cell lymphoma and that it activates the RHOA-VAV1 signaling, leading to the acceleration of T-cell signaling and the production of cytokines and chemokines.
RHOA mutations are a driver mutation in angioimmoblastic T cell lymphoma (AIT), and RHOA mutations lead to VAV1 activation.
RHOA mutations and VAV1 alterations may be the key drivers in the pathogenesis of AITL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RHOA G17V mutant is not a loss of function mutation but rather a gain of function mutation that is associated with increased T cell activation.
the VAV1 mutations or VAV1-STAP2 translocation may play a role in the development of angioimmoblastic T-cell Lymphoma.

RHOA mutations in AITL are not necessarily associated with the classical RHO signaling, and that VAV1 is the major effector molecule for G17V RHA in AITL, which may provide a novel therapeutic target in the future.
